implemented: A pure UMD motion-system contract owns deterministic attack, special and dodge poses for Panzer, Pun-Slinger and Gear Shepherd.
Panzer uses a heavy crouch-to-overhead pan slam; Pun-Slinger uses recoil and bread-fan motion; Gear Shepherd uses a conductor-style command sweep.
Every hero exposes version-1 semantic root, body, head, left arm, right arm, legs, weapon and action-cue bindings for later skeletal-rig replacement.
Local player two uses the same tested motion path independently of player one.
Reduced motion removes locomotion bounce and pose travel while retaining a static class-colored action cue.
Combat damage timing and balance remain immediate and unchanged; this seam is presentation-only.

live.claim: Each class has a distinct readable comedy-action silhouette.
live.observed: Panzer displayed a gold pan-slam arc, Pun-Slinger displayed a teal impact cue with a seven-bread fan, and Gear Shepherd displayed a violet conductor sweep. The semantic phase was impact or recovery during each observed action and settled afterward.

live.claim: Local shared-screen player two owns an independent attack pose.
live.observed: After moving P2 clear of the Human Panzer, slash input produced a Toon Pun-Slinger impact pose and teal cue while the hero remained settled; P2 then returned to settled.

live.claim: Reduced motion preserves feedback without animated pose travel.
live.observed: With Reduced motion checked, attack exposed the reduced-cue semantic phase and a compact gold cue while the Human Panzer retained the base stance. The action returned to settled.

limitations: Production Blender rigs, facial animation and authored attack clips remain unavailable; procedural geometry is still the visual substrate.
The rolling-frame capability was unavailable. Exact phase durations and ordering are deterministic test evidence, not screenshot-timed claims.
Physical gamepad feel and long-session human readability remain outside this bounded pass.
